summary.headline: Allcargo Global Q2 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR4,320 crore; EBITDA hit INR122 crore and PAT returned to INR32 crore profit.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 27% YoY and 23% QoQ to INR4,320 crore on elevated freight rates, while volumes declined YoY across LCL, FCL and air. Gross profit rose 21% YoY to INR837 crore and EBITDA rose to INR122 crore from INR37 crore a year earlier, with staff and admin costs flat QoQ and YoY. PAT of INR32 crore marked a return to profitability versus losses in both Q2 FY26 and Q1 FY27. Management attributed roughly 20-30% of the gains to industry freight tailwinds and about 70% to its own business initiatives, and said freight rates are expected to soften gradually. Net debt rose marginally to INR587 crore from INR571 crore on higher working capital.

segments.name: LCL
segments.commentary: Volume down 5.7% YoY but up 2.9% QoQ (management cites about 3% QoQ growth); management says it likely held or gained market share. Global market leader in LCL.

segments.name: FCL
segments.commentary: Volume down 12% YoY and up 1.3% QoQ; about 650,000 TEUs of FCL business handled. Management cites West Asia market decline.

segments.name: Air freight
segments.commentary: Volume down 10% YoY but up 16% QoQ (management also cites over 15% sequential growth); positioned as an emerging product.

guidance_outlook: Normalised volume growth target of mid-single digit, about 6-7% for both LCL and FCL, assuming industry growth of 5-6% LCL and 3-4% FCL.
Management says geopolitical resolution could add about 2 pp to LCL and 3-4 pp to FCL growth; not in base case.
Gross profit target of INR900-1,000 crore per quarter over the next couple of years; management says the cost base will be held flat.
Reiterated consistent annualised EBITDA target of about INR500 crore; company says it is ahead of plan due to tailwinds but expects to be on guidance for CY2027.
Freight rates expected to soften gradually over the next four to five months; management expects Q3 onward to be at par or ahead of guidance, with Q4 (Jan-Mar) seasonally weak.
Under consideration: change of financial year to calendar year ending December 2026, subject to approvals.
Bad-debt provision expected to be finalised by December 2026 quarter-end, with normalisation from January 2027.
capex_capacity: Business described as asset-light with no significant capex; depreciation mostly goodwill amortisation from past acquisitions.
No new acquisitions foreseen in the near term; management expects depreciation to decline.
Warehouses and CFS facilities are leased or third-party contracted, mainly used in LCL.
Management expects lower effective tax rate and cash taxes as loss-making geographies turn profitable and tax losses are utilised.
demand_pricing: Freight rates rose on capacity constraints, peak-season demand, port congestion and West Asia disruption; Middle East lanes remain most impacted while transpacific and transatlantic rates have softened somewhat.
Management says the freight rate increase more than offset volume loss, providing a yield and profitability tailwind.
DSO about 46-47 days; receivables and supplier payables both rose with volumes and freight rates.
Management said it is generally ahead of guidance by two to three quarters, attributing this to industry tailwinds.
Management is focusing on exiting loss-making trade lanes and boxes, which it says will mean lower volume growth but higher profitability impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is the YoY volume decline industry-wide or market share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline mainly to market contraction in West Asia; LCL held up better because FCL and air are more concentrated there. Management said it likely maintained or gained share on both YoY and QoQ bases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume and profitability guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Normalised volume growth target of 6-7% for LCL and FCL; a more conservative volume blend is expected with higher profitability impact. Management said 20-30% of gains come from industry tailwinds and 70% from business initiatives.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 FY27 a new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the longer horizon should be at par or ahead of guidance, but the next one to two quarters may be volatile as freight tailwinds fade. Q3 is seen as more visible and Jan-Mar typically seasonally weak.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue reach INR20,000 crore over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue is a derivative of freight rates and gross profit is the focus. It targets INR900-1,000 crore of quarterly gross profit in a couple of years, with costs held flat.

qa_highlights.question: Can staff and admin costs fall in absolute terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to hold costs flat in a blended USD, EUR and INR basket. Staff and admin costs fell about 8% in USD terms YoY, and further reductions are not the explicit target.

qa_highlights.question: Why can't the company cut employee costs as sharply as DSV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its LCL consolidation model differs from DSV's acquisition-led synergy approach; SG&A costs in USD terms are down about 8% YoY and the current aim is to hold costs flat.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bad-debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current bad-debt charge reflects historical clean-up tied to Middle East businesses shut down; the provision is expected to be finalised by the December quarter, with normalisation from January. The FY27 number was not provided.

risks_watch: Freight-rate normalisation could reduce the 20-30% of gains attributed to industry tailwinds; management says a single quarter cannot recoup this.
Bad-debt charges from closed Middle East businesses; the provision is expected to be finalised by December 2026 quarter-end and the FY27 total was not disclosed.
Proposed change in financial year to calendar year ending December 2026 is subject to approvals.
West Asia geopolitical disruption and port congestion continue to weigh on volumes, particularly FCL and air.
Working capital intensity: DSO of 46-47 days and rising receivables, with net debt up slightly QoQ.
Seasonal Jan-Mar quarter is expected to be weak; management could not yet predict its outcome.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and cost discipline, but cautious and hedged on freight-rate durability and near-term quarters. Management repeatedly said outcomes depend on geopolitical developments outside its control and declined to give a FY27 bad-debt number.
key_quotes: So, while there could be a negative impact on the volumes due to some of these disruptions, in general, the freight rate increase more than offset that impact and creates a tailwind on the yield and profitability.
Most encouragingly, staff and admin costs remained largely flat, Q-On-Q and year-on-year, with the company's focus on cost.
So, I think we can target mid-single-digit numbers 6% to 7% kind of growth on volume terms for both LCL and FCL.
At this point in time, if you look at the gains, potentially 20%-30% of the gains are contributed by the industry tailwind, 70% is coming in from the business initiatives.

growth.why: Management targets normalised volume growth of 6-7% for LCL and FCL and gross profit of INR900-1,000 crore per quarter over two years, but backing is vague: no capacity additions (asset-light, no significant capex), and the near-term gains are mostly freight-rate driven, with rates expected to soften over the next four to five months.

Bad-debt clean-up tied to closed Middle East businesses; FY27 total not disclosed, provision to be finalised by Dec 2026 quarter

quality.why: Revenue grew 27% YoY on freight rates, not volume: LCL -5.7%, FCL -12%, air -10% YoY, with management attributing 20-30% of gains to temporary industry freight tailwinds that are expected to soften, while the bad-debt charge from closed Middle East businesses is undisclosed for FY27.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 2.8% in Q2 FY27 from 1.1% a year ago, but management says freight tailwinds (20-30% of gains) will soften over the next four to five months and Q4 (Jan-Mar) is seasonally weak.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Asset-light model with no significant capex; warehouses and CFS are leased or third-party, and no new acquisitions are foreseen near term.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Normalised target of 6-7% for LCL and FCL versus industry growth of 5-6% LCL and 3-4% FCL, but Q2 volumes were down 5.7% (LCL) and 12% (FCL) YoY and management is exiting loss-making lanes.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says it has no significant capex and utilisation is not discussed; asset-light model means no capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says it is ahead of plan by two to three quarters and that a geopolitical resolution could add about 2 pp to LCL and 3-4 pp to FCL growth, but that is not in the base case.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects freight rates to soften over four to five months and says the next one to two quarters may be volatile, with Q4 seasonally weak and bad-debt provisions still to be finalised by December 2026 quarter-end.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launches were discussed; air freight is described only as an emerging product with 16% QoQ volume growth.

rows.label: Flat staff and admin cost base
rows.why: Management aims to hold the USD cost base flat while expanding gross profit to INR900-1,000 crore per quarter; SG&A in USD was already down about 8% YoY.

rows.label: Gross profit target INR900-1,000 crore per quarter
rows.why: Q2 FY27 gross profit was INR837 crore, so the target needs about 8-20% more, and it depends on freight rates that management expects to soften.

rows.label: Change of financial year to calendar year
rows.why: Under consideration, with the year-end moving to December 2026, but still subject to approvals.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost discipline and margin gains and said it is ahead of plan, but cautious and hedged on freight-rate durability, near-term volatility and the bad-debt charge, and declined to give a FY27 number.
